pr_body:
Instead of using raw TCP sockets and parsing HTTP requests manually which is tends to be quite error-prone, we can create an HTTP proxy server using ApacheHttpServer. In contrast to `com.sun.net` an Apache HTTP server it can act as an HTTP proxy. 

This change also allows the server to upport persistent keep-alive connections. It should prevent creating excessive threads to handle new HTTP connection which matters when we run heavy tests in `GcsProxyIntegrationTests.`

It's a more straighforward alternative to #93891.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93824
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93811
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93816

review_comments: I think we should declare the apache httpclient as an explicit test dependency, it is not declared in the gcs module.
Why are we excluding the Content-Lenght headers?
`ApacheHTTPClient`sets `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` header itself based on the request's body and doesn't allow the user to set it explicitly.

I believe we don't need to do that, that's why `TreeSet` was created with the `CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER` comparator. The comparator will make sure that headers in different cases correspond to the same value, so a `contains` call on the `content-length` string will return `true`.
